scores.claim_text: ASTS entered a contract with the U.S. SDA through a prime contractor with total expected revenue of $43.0 million to provide certain testing services utilizing the initial BB satellites.

pentagon_jbook_by_contractor.note: AST SpaceMobile not indexed as primary contractor on any J-Book PE in corpus

pentagon_jbook_sda_transport.replacement_program: Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone / Space Link

scores.interpretation: The $43M expected revenue is described as flowing 'through a prime contractor' for 'testing services utilizing the initial BB satellites'. The largest SDA-side recipient program — the Transport Layer program of record (PE 1206410SF) — is UNFUNDED for the second consecutive year per the J-Book corpus and is being replaced by SDN, sole-sourced to SpaceX/Starshield. ASTS itself is not listed as a primary contractor on any J-Book PE in the corpus, and direct USAspending DoD obligations to 'AST SpaceMobile' / 'AST & Science' / 'SpaceMobile' = $0. That is consistent with the $43M being a sub-contract; the past performance is plausible (BB1-5 launched and tested with U.S. government for non-communication apps). The risk is forward extension: the SDA program of record that would absorb new task orders for satellite-comms testing is unfunded and folded into SpaceX-sole-sourced SDN. Scoring MODERATE: the $43M is largely past/recognized revenue under existing PO; the forward narrative ('utilizing the initial BB satellites' for the U.S. government) is structurally exposed.

scores.claim_text: ASTS has an agreement directly with the U.S. SDA for the Europa Track 2 commercial solutions program with a total contract value of approximately $30.0 million.

pentagon_jbook_sda_t3_transport.replacement_program: Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone (sole-sourced to SpaceX/Starshield)

pentagon_jbook_sdn_by_name.note: SDN is the replacement architecture but Pentagon has stated single-vendor (SpaceX/Starshield) with no binding second-vendor commitment

scores.interpretation: This is the load-bearing J-Book divergence finding. ASTS asserts a DIRECT SDA contract on 'Europa Track 2 commercial solutions program' worth $30M, AND that SHIELD/IDIQ at MDA + the $43M sub-contract together represent the forward DoD pipeline. The Signal-OS corpus shows: (a) the SDA satellite-comms program-of-record line item (Tranche 3 Transport Layer, PE 1206410SF) is UNFUNDED for FY2025-FY2027; (b) per corpus notes the SDA is being DISSOLVED as a standalone agency, with requirements rolled into the Space Data Network backbone; (c) the SDN replacement (PE 1203636SF) is sole-sourced to SpaceX / Starshield with Pentagon stating only non-binding intent to add a second vendor. ASTS's BB constellation directly competes with the Starshield architecture but is NOT the named contractor on the replacement PE. The $30M Europa Track 2 itself is not in the corpus (NOT_FOUND — possible coverage gap, treat with caution) but the entire SDA umbrella is unfunded/being absorbed, and direct USAspending shows ZERO DoD obligations to ASTS by recipient name. Per heuristic 6 (USAspending cross-check: if pentagon_jbook says UNFUNDED AND usaspending shows ZERO obligations under the claimed program → RED_FLAG). The narrative-load is severe: the company's DoD pipeline beyond the booked $73M is dependent on a contracting authority that the J-Book corpus indicates is being dissolved in favor of a sole-source incumbent. RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE.

scores.claim_text: ASTS received an IDIQ contract award on the Scalable Homeland Innovative Enterprise Layered Defense (SHIELD) program, enabling it to pursue future task orders under MDA's multi-award framework.

pentagon_jbook_shield_by_name.note: SHIELD acronym not indexed in corpus — possible coverage gap

scores.interpretation: The SHIELD IDIQ claim is intrinsically a PIPELINE claim — no ceiling disclosed, no task orders disclosed, and 'enables us to pursue future task orders' is explicit forward language. SHIELD itself is not in the J-Book corpus (NOT_FOUND); the most likely host PE in the MDA J-Book is the Ballistic Missile Defense System Space Programs PE 1206895C, which is FUNDED_SHRINKING (FY24 $107.6M → FY26 $97.1M). The broader MDA enabling PE 0603890C is FUNDED_STEADY. No earmark sub-signal. Heuristic 2 applies: future / not-booked + materially uncertain host PE → downgrade to MODERATE. USAspending shows zero direct DoD obligations to ASTS, which is consistent with the claim itself ('enables us to pursue future task orders' — i.e., no obligations yet). The risk to investors is that SHIELD IDIQ awards being announced without a host PE in the FY26 J-Book + shrinking BMD-Space funding makes the forward pipeline uncertain even if the IDIQ vehicle is real.

scores.claim_text: FY 2025 services revenue of $26.5M was mainly attributable to performance obligations under agreements with the U.S. government either directly or through prime contractors; ASTS intends to continue generating DoD services revenue from BB satellites.

usaspending_ast_llc.note: substring matches to OTHER 'AST LLC' entities — top awards are Mountain West Precast (F-35 hangar construction), Overseas Shipholding, Superior Construction — NOT AST SpaceMobile subsidiary

scores.interpretation: $26.5M of FY2025 services revenue is described as DoD-derived, but ZERO direct DoD obligations show up in USAspending for any recognizable ASTS entity name (the 113 'AST LLC' matches are substring false-positives for unrelated firms). This is most consistent with revenue flowing entirely through a prime contractor (sub-tier obligation, invisible in recipient-name USAspending) — which is consistent with the C1 'through a prime contractor' language. However, the forward narrative ('intend to generate additional services revenue from BB satellites for the U.S. government') is rated against a J-Book that shows the most-relevant SDA program-of-record is unfunded (see C2). Per heuristic 6: past revenue real (booked $26.5M) but the forward pipeline is structurally weakened. Scoring MODERATE rather than SEVERE because (a) $26.5M is only ~37% of FY25 revenue, not majority concentration, and (b) the prime-contractor pathway means specific PE identification is partial.

scores.claim_text: ASTS expects to 'secure additional contracts with the U.S. government or its prime contractors for non-commercial use of our BB satellites' as a forward business pillar.
scores.interpretation: The forward 'additional DoD contracts' claim is the kind of soft pipeline statement that anchors valuation but doesn't name a PE. Searching plausible host PEs in the J-Book corpus: Commercial Services is borderline (FUNDED_STEADY but ~24% smaller than FY24), Tactically Responsive Space is SHRINKING, SSPT is SHRINKING. Aggregate signal across the most-relevant Space Force commercial / responsive PE pool is downward, not flat or growing. Per heuristic 1 and 2: shrinking host PEs + forward narrative-load → MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY. The claim is not falsified (the PEs are funded and ASTS could win task orders), but the budget-line trajectory is contracting, not expanding.

scores.claim_text: ASTS positions its BB constellation for transport-layer-style satellite communications applications adjacent to the SDA PWSA pipeline.

pentagon_jbook_t3_transport_layer.replacement_program: Space Data Network (SDN) Backbone / Space Link

pentagon_jbook_narrowband_satcom.note: growing but ASTS not listed as participant in corpus

scores.interpretation: ASTS positions its BB constellation as a candidate for SDA Transport Layer-type missions (direct-to-cellular, beyond-line-of-sight comms). The J-Book corpus shows: (a) Tranche 3 Transport Layer is UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS and is being replaced by SDN sole-sourced to SpaceX/Starshield; (b) ASTS is NOT named as a primary contractor on T3 or T0-T2 (those are York/Lockheed/Northrop); (c) Narrowband SatCom PE 1203109SF is growing, but ASTS is not in the corpus as a participant. Per heuristic 1: UNFUNDED_TWO_PLUS_YEARS on the host PE → SEVERE; per heuristic 3 (reorganization caveat) the replacement IS in corpus and is sole-source to a competitor (SpaceX), so the funding has not 'moved to ASTS'. Downgrade from RED to SEVERE because the adjacency claim is implicit (not an explicit revenue tie) — but the forward government-use pillar of ASTS's narrative is contradicted by the J-Book: the line of business the company is positioning toward (mil-grade direct-to-device transport) is being concentrated with a sole-source incumbent that is not ASTS.

scores.claim_text: ASTS owns approximately 3,850 patent and patent pending claims worldwide, of which approximately 1,900 have been officially granted or allowed; 38 patent families with terms starting in 2039.

uspto_ast_science.note: core legal-entity name; sample patents are direct-to-cell / phased-array satcom — clearly the real ASTS portfolio

scores.interpretation: The 3,850-claim, 1,900-granted figure is a CLAIMS count (a single patent typically has 15-30 claims). USPTO ODP returns 56 granted U.S. patents for 'AST & Science' (the operating LLC), which at ~20 claims/patent maps to ~1,100 U.S. claims — meaningfully below 1,900 but plausibly explained by the worldwide / 38-family figure (foreign jurisdictions, allowed-but-not-granted claims). USPTO ODP doesn't index multi-token assignee names well so this is a directional check only. Not a J-Book claim. Score MODERATE because the U.S.-only USPTO read-through is materially smaller than the headline number but the claim explicitly says 'worldwide' and 'claims' (not patents). Control claim — not the primary signal.

summary.headline_finding: ASTS names SDA as a direct customer ($30M Europa Track 2) and via prime ($43M testing services) plus SHIELD/MDA IDIQ; J-Book corpus indicates SDA Transport Layer-of-record is UNFUNDED for 2+ consecutive years and is being replaced by SDN sole-sourced to SpaceX/Starshield. ASTS is not named as a contractor on any host J-Book PE in the corpus. Direct USAspending DoD obligations to AST SpaceMobile / AST & Science / SpaceMobile recipient names = $0 across 2020-2026. The DoD pipeline that ASTS's forward narrative anchors on (beyond the already-booked $26.5M FY25 services revenue) is structurally exposed.
